topics.model: This happened about six years ago and I still think about it. I'd left my purse on a bus, with everything in it, and I only realised twenty minutes later outside the supermarket. I was completely [[at a loss|5]], standing there checking the same pocket four times. Then a man I'd never seen before came running down the street with it in his hand. [[A complete stranger|2]], who'd got off two stops later, gone back, asked the driver, and then walked for fifteen minutes to find me. He didn't wait to be thanked properly; he [[offered to help|3]] and then simply went, [[without a second thought|6]]. That one small [[act of kindness|4]] genuinely [[restored my faith in people|7]]. I'm [[eternally grateful|9]], and ever since I've tried to [[pay it forward|8]] whenever somebody near me clearly needs [[helping out|1]].

words.mean: to help someone who is in difficulty
words.ex: Helping someone out takes ten minutes and they remember it for ten years.

words.mean: someone you have never met before
words.ex: A complete stranger ran fifteen minutes down the road to give it back.

words.mean: to say you're willing to give help
words.ex: Nobody else offered to help, and then suddenly somebody did.

words.mean: a kind thing someone does, often for no reason
words.ex: One small act of kindness can change how you see a whole city.

words.mean: to have no idea what to do next
words.ex: I was at a loss on the pavement, checking the same empty pocket repeatedly.

words.mean: immediately, without stopping to consider
words.ex: He handed it over without a second thought and disappeared into the crowd.

words.w: to restore your faith in people
words.mean: to make you believe again that people are good
words.ex: That afternoon restored my faith in people for about a decade.

words.mean: to help someone new instead of repaying the person who helped you
words.ex: I couldn't thank him properly, so I try to pay it forward instead.

words.mean: to feel thankful to someone forever
words.ex: I'm eternally grateful to a man whose name I never even asked.

topics.q: Talk about something you learned the hard way.
plan: Say what the lesson was in one sentence
Tell the story of how you learned it
Say what you do differently now
topics.model: Back everything up, and never assume tomorrow will be quieter. I [[learned that the hard way|4]] about eight years ago. I'd spent a whole term writing materials for a new course, all of it on one laptop, and I'd been meaning to copy it somewhere safe for weeks. People had told me to. I [[ignored the advice|3]] because I was busy, and I kept [[leaving it to the last minute|2]]. Then the laptop died on a Sunday evening, four days before the course started, and I lost the lot. I was [[caught out|6]] completely, and I had [[only myself to blame|8]]. That fortnight was grim: rewriting everything at night, [[cutting it fine|5]] with every deadline. It was an expensive [[lesson|1]], but it stuck. [[Once bitten, twice shy|9]]: now everything saves itself automatically, and I still check.

words.mean: to understand something important through experience
words.ex: I learned a lesson that fortnight that no amount of advice had taught me.

words.w: to leave something to the last minute
words.mean: to delay something until there's almost no time left
words.ex: I leave far too many things to the last minute and call it working well under pressure.

words.mean: to not listen to what people tell you to do
words.ex: Three people told me to make copies, and I ignored the advice every time.

words.w: to learn something the hard way
words.mean: to learn by making a painful mistake yourself
words.ex: Some things you only learn the hard way, however often you're warned.

words.mean: to leave yourself barely enough time
words.ex: I cut it fine with every deadline that month and slept about four hours a night.

words.mean: to be in trouble because you weren't prepared
words.ex: I was caught out completely, four days before a course I'd promised to run.

words.w: to come back to bite you
words.mean: to cause you problems later because of what you didn't do
words.ex: Putting it off for six weeks came back to bite me on a Sunday evening.

words.w: to have only yourself to blame
words.mean: to be responsible for your own problem
words.ex: I had only myself to blame, which is the least comforting thought available.

words.mean: after one bad experience you're careful the next time
words.ru: обжёгшись на молоке, дуешь на воду
words.ex: Once bitten, twice shy: everything I write now saves itself in three places.
